text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended lower on pre-weekend long liquidation. By the close, September was down $29 at $1,615 per tonne, while November closed $31 lower at $1,615 per tonne. In contrast to the arabica sector, there is no shortage of robusta coffee.

Arabica futures in New York bounced back from early lows to end mixed, as local short-covering and light commission house buying erased most of the day's losses. The September/December switch narrowed to 28.00 cents/lb compared with 32.55 cents/lb on the close on Thursday. The decline was ascribed as mainly technical although forecasts calling for cooler temperatures in Brazil in the middle of next week, lent some support to the market and prevented prices from slipping further.

Physical trade remains slow as many roasters continued to stick to the sidelines. September's hefty 28 cents/lb premium to second-month December and firm spot differentials continued to hinder prompt business. The market can be expected to remain firm through the September delivery. September gave up 2.95 cents/lb to close at 205.85 cents/lb. December closed 1.60 cents/lb lower at 177.85 cents/lb.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings for the week ended August 2, 1997 totalled approximately 365,000 60-kg bags, up from 315,000 bags the previous week and compared with 340,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 9,930 million 60-kg bags vs 9.825 million bags in the same year-ago period.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 3,190 bags as of August 7 to 94,119 bags. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.

CANADA - Canada imported 266,952 bags of coffee in April 1997, 11 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 1.003 million bags, nearly 12 percent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 9 per cent to 2.739 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/April 1997 were Guatemala (108,400 vs 95,700 bags), Brazil (109,300 vs 38,200 bags) and Colombia (134,000 vs 163,200 bags).

The country exported 153,300 bags of coffee in January/April 1997, 44 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 18 per cent to 357,800 bags.
